content.text:
Claude Code is an npm package (`@anthropic-ai/claude-code`), so `~/.local/bin/claude` means it was installed via npm, likely with:

```bash
npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
```

**1. To upgrade in place:**
```bash
npm update -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
```
or to force the absolute latest:
```bash
npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@latest
```

**2. Homebrew option:**

Claude Code is available via Homebrew:
```bash
brew install claude
```

Whether to switch is a matter of preference. Homebrew pros: easier upgrades via `brew upgrade`, managed alongside other tools. Cons: Homebrew tends to lag a day or two behind npm releases, so if you want `@latest` immediately, npm is faster.

**To switch to Homebrew cleanly:**
```bash
npm uninstall -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
brew install claude
```

For staying on the cutting edge, npm is the better choice since `@latest` is always current there. Homebrew is fine if you don't mind minor version lag and prefer a unified upgrade workflow (`brew upgrade` for everything).
